_comment: FactoryForge tag id -> absolute S7 address inside the FF_IO datablock, for the snap7 driver. DBX<byte>.<bit> for a Bool, DBD<byte> for a DInt or Real. These are the addresses TIA shows in the DB's Offset column.
_usage: .\factoryforge-sidecar connect --driver s7-snap7 -o host 192.168.1.20 -o db <FF_IO's DB number> --mapping examples/snap7_mapping.json
_usage_linux: ./factoryforge-sidecar connect --driver s7-snap7 -o host 192.168.1.20 -o db <FF_IO's DB number> --mapping examples/snap7_mapping.json
_requires: FF_IO must have 'Optimized block access' UNCHECKED (right-click the DB -> Properties -> Attributes), then recompiled and downloaded. An optimized DB has no absolute byte addresses at all, and snap7 cannot read it however correct this file is.
_layout: Matches examples/tia/FF_IO_datablock.md: eight Bools packed into byte 0, then two DInts. A DInt aligns to an even byte, so the first lands at byte 2 rather than byte 1, and the DB is 10 bytes total. VERIFIED against a live CPU. If you reorder the DB these move — check TIA's Offset column.
_note_invalid_address: 'Invalid address (0x05)' usually means the read ran off the end of the DB, not that the DB is optimized. FF_IO is 10 bytes; asking for 12 fails exactly that way.
_note_shared_bytes: Byte 0 holds both directions: bits 0-3 are PLC-written, bits 4-7 simulator-written. Bits are not individually addressable over S7, so writing a simulator bit means read-modify-write of a byte the PLC also writes. The driver keeps that window to a single byte, but if you are designing your own DB, put the two directions in different bytes and the race disappears.
_note_operator_tags: The operator and fault tags (panel.start/stop/reset/estop/setpoint, <drive>.fault) are deliberately NOT mapped here. This file matches examples/tia/FF_IO_datablock.md, whose byte layout was verified against a live CPU, and the ten tags below are the reference line's original I/O. To drive the panel or raise a fault from a real PLC, add the members to FF_IO yourself and extend this file — an unmapped tag is simply not exchanged, so nothing here breaks in the meantime.
